facts.raw_span: A man in his 60s with systemic sclerosis presented with a pruritic rash that had been present for 3 months
The patient denied any known preceding triggers or trauma to the area of the rash
He had tried treating with topical aloe, without improvement
Review of systems was negative for any new or worsening constitutional, respiratory, or gastrointestinal symptoms
Past medical history included heart failure, interstitial lung disease, sclerodactyly, and Raynaud phenomenon
He was receiving mycophenolate mofetil, 1 g twice daily
Examination findings were notable for firm, red-brown plaques without overlying scale on the proximal upper extremities and anterior trunk
There was no appreciable skin tightening in the affected areas
Complete blood cell count with differential was unremarkable

Lesional punch biopsy specimens showed nodular proliferations of thick collagen fibers in large fascicles, with one additionally showing homogeneous, brightly eosinophilic collagen bundles in haphazard array
Tissue cultures obtained by punch biopsy were negative for bacteria, fungus, and acid-fast bacillus
Firm, red-brown plaques without overlying scale on the proximal upper extremities and anterior trunk

concepts.why: The patient's presentation with a pruritic rash, firm red-brown plaques, and nodular proliferations of thick collagen fibers is consistent with NSF, a condition associated with systemic sclerosis and renal disease.
The patient's past medical history of systemic sclerosis, sclerodactyly, and Raynaud phenomenon, along with the presence of firm red-brown plaques, supports a diagnosis of scleroderma.
The patient's presentation with firm red-brown plaques without overlying scale, and the absence of appreciable skin tightening, is consistent with morphea, a form of localized scleroderma.
The patient's presentation with homogeneous, brightly eosinophilic collagen bundles in haphazard array, and the absence of infectious diseases, supports a diagnosis of eosinophilic fasciitis.

The patient's presentation with firm, red-brown plaques without overlying scale, and the absence of appreciable skin tightening, is consistent with lichen sclerosus, a condition that can present with similar skin lesions.

The patient's presentation with a pruritic rash, firm red-brown plaques, and nodular proliferations of thick collagen fibers, along with a history of systemic sclerosis, supports a diagnosis of scleromyxedema.

The patient's presentation with firm, red-brown plaques without overlying scale, and the absence of appreciable skin tightening, is consistent with pseudoscleroderma, a condition that can mimic scleroderma.
The patient's history of mycophenolate mofetil use and the presence of firm, red-brown plaques without overlying scale, supports a diagnosis of chronic graft-versus-host disease.
